label: Redispatch: when the market's flow does not fit the grid
context: Animate redispatch in Germany as a simple schematic of the country: a north node (wind farms, coast) and a south node (Bavaria/Baden-Wuerttemberg, industry) joined by a transmission corridor with capacity 5 GW. Phase 1 'The market clears': the single German bidding zone ignores internal lines; the day-ahead result schedules north wind 14 GW with northern demand 6 GW, and southern demand 13 GW served by southern plants 5 GW; so 8 GW should flow north to south; animate particles flowing along the corridor. Phase 2 'The line is overloaded': the corridor turns red, label '8 GW scheduled > 5 GW thermal limit (n-1 secure)'. Phase 3 'Redispatch': the TSO curtails 3 GW of northern wind (wind turbines dim, label 'curtailed, compensated: EUR'), and starts 3 GW of southern gas plants (plants light up, label 'ramped up, paid their costs'); the flow drops to 5 GW, corridor turns blue/ok; total supply unchanged. Phase 4 'Who pays': a counter shows costs; caption 'In 2025, congestion management cost about EUR 3.1 billion (BNetzA), paid via network charges; HVDC lines SuedLink (2028) and SuedOstLink (2027) are meant to widen the corridor'. Colours: ink #04204B, wind #0B4FC0, gas #B4552F, ok-flow #138374, overload #B4552F. Text >= 12 px, white background, phases ~5 s, loop.

spec.title: Redispatch: when the market's flow does not fit the grid
spec.caption: The single German bidding zone schedules 8 GW from north to south, but the corridor can carry only 5 GW. The TSO curtails 3 GW of northern wind and starts 3 GW of southern gas. Flow drops to 5 GW, total supply is unchanged, and the cost lands on network charges.
